question: One patient is diagnosed with a 4 cm lung cancer without pleural contact in the right upper lobe. The extension study reveals the presence of metastasis in right parahilar nodes, without evidence of distant metastasis. The staging of the tumor will be:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: 4 cm lung cancer -> no pleural contact -> presence of metastasis in right parahilar nodes -> no evidence of distant metastasis -> classified as Stage IIIB -> 85%
CHAIN: 4 cm lung cancer -> no pleural contact -> metastasis in regional lymph nodes -> classified as Stage IIIA -> 90%
CHAIN: 4 cm lung cancer -> no pleural contact -> right parahilar node involvement -> indicates advanced local disease -> classified as Stage IIB -> 80%
CHAIN: 4 cm lung cancer -> no pleural contact -> presence of metastasis in right parahilar nodes -> suggests regional spread -> classified as Stage IIIA -> 75%
analysis: The patient has a 4 cm lung cancer in the right upper lobe with metastasis to the right parahilar nodes. According to the TNM staging system, the presence of regional lymph node involvement (N1) indicates a higher stage. Since there is no distant metastasis (M0), this would classify the cancer as Stage IIB (T2a N1 M0).
